Primary request: A quiet present-day summer late-morning view of the Seine and the real Pont Royal in Paris. Reference image 1 is ONLY a structural reference for the real bridge, not an image to copy. Make a completely new full natural-color photograph.
Geography and camera: camera on the LEFT/SOUTH bank, Quai Anatole-France, about 90 metres downstream/west of Pont Royal, slightly elevated above the low quay, looking northeast across the river toward the bridge and the RIGHT/NORTH bank at the southeast edge of the Tuileries Garden. This is not a right-bank viewpoint. The bridge crosses diagonally from the near left-bank end at image right to the far right-bank end in the middle-left. Show all five masonry arches; the central arch is a little higher and wider, weathered pale stone piers and a simple solid stone parapet. On the far bank behind the bridge, a tree row leads leftward along the pale stone embankment toward the Tuileries Garden. Only a narrow sliver of the historic Pavillon de Flore at the far right edge; trees, bridge and water are the main subjects. Do not invent another palace across the opposite bank.

One tiny plain unmarked tourist boat far away, no visible passengers or faces. This exact camera position and bridge geometry must be reusable for an 1873 reconstruction.
Photography: ordinary natural soft summer morning, muted realistic greens and limestone, water grey-green with many irregular small ripples and imperfect reflections. Individual varied leaves rather than repeated tree balls. Subtle worn stone texture, no HDR, no illustration, no dramatic grading, no oversaturation or smooth plastic surfaces.
Avoid: any text, numbers, letters, signs, labels, logos, watermarks, frames, banners, billboards, murals, identifiable people, cars in foreground, modern sculptural furniture. No Louvre glass pyramid, Eiffel Tower, Sacré-Cœur, modern bridge, feeding birds, or busy scene. No reproduced artwork.
